subtopics.title: The Longitudinal Profile — A River Seen From the Side

questions.question: A longitudinal profile is:
options: A map of a river's drainage basin
A side view of a river from its source to its mouth
A cross-section taken straight across the channel
A list of the river's tributaries

questions.question: Which evidence identifies a GRADED longitudinal profile on a sketch?
options: A waterfall over resistant rock
A dam ponding the flow
A smooth, concave curve with no steps from source to mouth
A steep step near the mouth

questions.question: The permanent base level of a river is:
options: Sea level — the lowest level to which it can erode
The height of its largest waterfall
A dam wall along its course
The level of its source

questions.question: A dam and a band of resistant rock shown on an ungraded profile both act as:
options: Permanent base levels
Sources of the river
Signs of rejuvenation
Temporary base levels the river will eventually remove

subtopics.title: How a Meander Works — Two Banks, Two Jobs

questions.question: Meanders are more likely to form in the:
options: Upper course, on steep gradients
Source region, in the mountains
Lower course, on gentle gradients where lateral erosion dominates
Waterfall zone

questions.question: On the outside of a meander bend the water:
options: Moves fastest and erodes, undercutting the bank
Moves slowest and deposits sand
Stands still
Flows upstream

questions.question: The gentle inner bank of a meander is called the:
options: Undercut slope
Knickpoint
River cliff
Slip-off slope

questions.question: To account for the gentle gradient of an inner bank, the memorandum expects:
options: Erosion happens there because the water is fast
Deposition happens there because the water on the inside of the bend moves slowly
The bank is made of resistant rock
Vertical erosion deepens the channel there

questions.question: The meander neck narrows because:
options: Deposition builds it outward
The river dries up seasonally
Outer-bank erosion on both limbs of the loop eats into it from both sides
Vegetation grows across the channel

questions.question: The river finally breaks through the narrowed neck:
options: During a flood, when volume and energy are high
During the dry season, when the channel is empty
Only after a dam is built
When the sea level rises

questions.question: After the breakthrough, the cut-off loop becomes a separate oxbow lake because:
options: The loop erodes deeper than the new channel
The loop lifts above the floodplain
The water in the loop flows backwards
Deposition seals both ends of the abandoned loop, plugging it off from the new channel

questions.question: In old age, an oxbow lake that has silted up and been overgrown is called a:
options: Wind gap
Meander scar
Knickpoint
Point bar

subtopics.title: Reading Profiles and Meanders in the Exam

questions.question: On a longitudinal profile sketch, a vertical step over hatched resistant rock represents:
options: A waterfall interrupting an ungraded profile
The permanent base level
An oxbow lake
The river's source

questions.question: In a photograph of a meander, the outer bank can be recognised as:
options: A gentle bar of sand sloping into the water
A reed-covered crescent away from the channel
The steep, raw, collapsing bank on the fast side of the bend
The flattest part of the floodplain

questions.question: On a topographic map, an oxbow lake appears as:
options: A straight blue canal crossing the floodplain
A circular contour pattern on a hilltop
A dam symbol with a wall
A detached crescent of blue or marsh symbols beside a winding river

questions.question: Loops entrenched in deep gorges with contours crowded along both banks are:
options: Ordinary floodplain meanders
Incised meanders — old loops cut downward by rejuvenation
Oxbow lakes
Braided channels

subtopics.title: The Slide From the Mountain to the Sea

questions.question: In the playground-slide picture, the smooth swoop that starts steep and lands gently is the:
options: Ungraded profile
Cross-section of a valley
Graded profile every river works towards
Drainage basin

questions.question: The ledge on the unfinished slide stands for:
options: A waterfall over hard rock the river has not yet worn through
The river's mouth
An oxbow lake
The floodplain

questions.question: The sea acts as the floor at the bottom of the slide because:
options: Rivers flow fastest at the coast
Waves erode the river's source
The sea is warmer than the river
No river can erode below the level of the sea it empties into

questions.question: A narrow, deep V-shaped valley cross-section on a profile sketch signals:
options: The lower course, where the river swings sideways
The upper course, where the young river cuts straight down
An oxbow lake in old age
A dam behind a wall

questions.question: In the taxi picture, the passenger by the far window shows how water on the outside of a bend:
options: Travels the long path fast, giving it energy to erode
Travels the short path slowly
Stops moving completely
Swaps places with the inside water

questions.question: The cliff outside, beach inside pairing matches which exam terms?
options: Knickpoint outside, terrace inside
Slip-off slope outside, undercut slope inside
Undercut slope outside, slip-off slope inside
Waterfall outside, rapids inside

questions.question: The meander loop wanders across the valley floor over the years because:
options: The floodplain tilts the channel sideways
Wind pushes the water off course
Earthquakes shift the channel
Each flood digs the outer cliff further out while the inner beach follows behind

subtopics.title: The Shortcut Through the Empty Plot

questions.question: The two roadworks crews trenching towards each other represent:
options: Deposition building up both banks
Outer-bank erosion attacking the meander neck from both sides
Two tributaries joining the river
The river splitting into a delta

questions.question: The main current abandons the loop after the breakthrough because the shortcut is:
options: Steeper, straighter and faster than the long way round
Deeper than the sea
Blocked by vegetation
Colder than the loop

questions.question: The gates of sand in the story are:
options: Dunes blown in from the coast
The walls of a dam
Bridges across the river
Deposition sealing the two ends of the abandoned loop

questions.question: The correct order for the eight-step oxbow paragraph is:
options: Neck narrows → outer banks eroded → lake dries → flood breakthrough
Flood breakthrough → neck narrows → outer banks eroded → ends sealed
Outer banks eroded → inner banks built → neck narrows → flood breakthrough → shortcut adopted → ends sealed → oxbow lake → meander scar
Ends sealed → shortcut adopted → neck narrows → outer banks eroded
